question: A store had 147 items. They added 80 items in restocking. They subtracted 40 items sold. They subtracted 174 items for bulk order fulfillment. Finally, 8 items were removed for quality check. Using the word 'double', between Jennifer (inventory control) and Marcus (receiving), how many items are tracked?

A warehouse had 126 items. They subtracted 75 items sold. They multiplied by 4 to plan inventory. They added 39 more items. Finally, 234 items were deducted for fulfillment. Between Michael (operations) and Rebecca (inventory), how many items remain?

A farm had 117 bushels. They divided by 3 for equal distribution. They subtracted 21 bushels used. They multiplied by 7 for a week projection. Finally, 4 bushels were removed for quality control. Tracking from morning harvest through evening inventory, how many bushels remain?

A bakery started with 39 pastries. They added 4 pastries from a special order. They added 14 more pastries. They multiplied by 7 for display planning. They added 48 more pastries. Finally, they multiplied by 9 for a projected sales day. Using minutes and hours for time conversion, how many pastries are projected?

A store had 26 items initially. They added 20 items from restocking. They multiplied by 4 for a weekly display plan. They multiplied by 5 for customer projection. Finally, they divided by 4 for equal distribution among departments. Using the word 'half', between Marcus (morning) and Elena (evening managing displays), how many items per section?

A factory had 217 units. They multiplied by 3 for production. They subtracted 626 units completed. They subtracted 4 units removed by error. They multiplied by 3 for next-phase planning. Then by 3 again for comprehensive timeline. Finally, they doubled for a two-week projection. Using a morning-through-evening schedule, how many units are planned?

A school had 12 desks initially. They added 6 desks in the morning. They subtracted 12 desks sent to repair. They added 64 desks from donations. They multiplied by 9 for an assembly. Finally, 165 desks were deducted for other schools. Using hours instead of desks, how many desks remain for the classroom?

A warehouse had 179 packages. They subtracted 50 packages delivered. They added 3 packages returned. They multiplied by 9 for volume projection. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for expanded planning. Using minutes as time conversion with a distractor about external factors, what is the final package projection?

A storage facility had 100 items. They divided by 4 for location distribution. They subtracted 2 items for cleanup. They added 8 items from new stock. They added 15 more items. Finally, 7 items were removed. Using minutes and hours as measurement, how many items are distributed?

A farm had 208 acres. They multiplied by 6 to plan expansion. They added 35 acres. They multiplied by 8 to account for all zones. They multiplied by 2 for a comprehensive assessment. Finally, they multiplied by 5 for a full-year projection. Using the word 'twice', how many acres are in the annual land management plan?

A supplier had 117 items. They multiplied by 5 for inventory tracking. They added 13 items from new stock. They multiplied by 7 for a weekly projection. They subtracted 3840 items due to a major fulfillment. They multiplied by 3 for follow-up orders. Finally, 808 items were deducted for returns. Using the word 'triple', how many items remain?

A store had 158 items. They added 35 items from restocking. They added 8 more items. They multiplied by 6 for weekly planning. They added 36 items. Finally, they multiplied by 4 for monthly projection. A separate warehouse had 75 items but that was not included. Using minutes and hours conversion, how many items are projected?

A factory had 73 units. They multiplied by 6 for production. Then by 7 to account for shifts. Then by 6 for facility capacity. Finally by 5 for expansion planning. They subtracted 49252 units from a major shipment. Then they multiplied by 2 for next-week projection. From morning through evening inventory tracking, how many units are counted?

A clinic had 142 patient files. They subtracted 140 files sent to archive. They added 53 files from new patients. They subtracted 9 files for deletion. They multiplied by 5 for quarterly records. Finally, 65 files were added as amendments. Using the word 'half', how many active patient files does the clinic have?

A warehouse had 165 boxes. They subtracted 155 boxes for fulfillment. They added 73 boxes from new shipments. They multiplied by 4 for storage planning. They added 27 more boxes. They multiplied by 6 for comprehensive tracking. Finally, 450 boxes were deducted. Using the word 'half', how many boxes remain?

A project started with 31 tasks. They subtracted 17 tasks completed. They multiplied by 4 for team expansion. They subtracted 34 tasks cancelled. They added 15 tasks recovered. Finally, 34 more tasks were removed. Using one distractor about external project factors and tracking through morning and evening, how many active tasks remain?

A store started with 62 items. They added 14 items in the morning. They added 60 items in the afternoon. They added 35 more items. Finally, they multiplied by 3 for a projected daily total. From morning through afternoon and evening inventory checks with Nathan and Paula, how many items are projected?

A bakery started with 25 loaves. They multiplied by 8 for morning production. Then by 6 for full-day output. They added 78 loaves from the afternoon shift. Finally, 4 loaves were added from overtime. Between Marcus (morning baker) and Jennifer (afternoon baker), how many loaves total?

A store had 206 items initially. They added 79 items from morning restocking. They added 39 items in afternoon deliveries. They added 67 more items. They added 71 additional items. Finally, 19 more items were added and then 76 more. Through morning, afternoon, and evening tracking, how many items are in final inventory?

A factory had 147 units. They multiplied by 6 to track production. Then by 2 for shift coverage. They added 78 units from extra production. They subtracted 507 units completed. They added 73 units from rework. Finally, 103 units were deducted for quality assurance. Using hours and minutes conversion, what is the final active unit count?

A supplier had 37 units. They added 55 units from new stock. They multiplied by 5 for volume projection. They divided by 2 to allocate to two facilities. They added 29 units as amendments. They added 33 more units. Finally, 11 units were added. Using minutes and hours conversion, between Paul and Diana managing distribution, how many units total?

A store had 87 items. They subtracted 3 damaged items. They subtracted 68 more items sold. They multiplied by 3 for replacement plan. They added 16 items from restocking. Finally, 32 items were added as amendment. One nearby store had 45 extra items but those were not included. Between Marcus and Elena managing inventory, how many items total?

A library had 34 books initially. They added 9 books in the morning. They subtracted 17 books checked out. They added 30 books returned. Finally, 5 books were added from a donation. Using minutes and hours as conversion, how many books are in circulation?

A warehouse started with 95 items. They multiplied by 9 for inventory assessment. They subtracted 438 items fulfilled. They added 54 items from new delivery. Finally, 114 items were deducted for returns. Using the word 'half', between Steven (morning) and Nicole (evening), how many items are managed?

A store had 213 items. They subtracted 62 items sold. They multiplied by 8 for weekly projection. They added 42 items from restocking. Finally, 9 items were added as amendments. Using one distractor about a separate location with 28 items, and the question asked about an intermediate quantity's final state, how many items are tracked?
